title: Can You Trust Ancestry DNA Kits?

blanks.sentence: A family tree is a diagram showing all the members of a _____.
Ancestry refers to the origins of your _____.
DNA is passed down from parents to _____.
Chris wondered whether his results should be taken with a pinch of _____.
Humans share _____ of their DNA with each other.
Forebears are relatives who lived in the _____.
Ethnicity is closely connected to a geographical _____.
Greg sent DNA samples to two different _____.
The second test said Greg was 66% north and west _____.
If something blows your mind, it makes you excited or _____.

multipleChoice.question: What is the programme mainly discussing?
options: How to draw a family tree by hand
How accurate DNA ancestry tracing can be
How to change your surname
How to store historical documents

multipleChoice.question: Why did Chris question his DNA ancestry test?
options: The results broadly matched expectations but included some glitches
The company refused to send him any result
He had never sent a sample to the company
The test only showed his surname

multipleChoice.question: What does it mean to take something with a pinch of salt?
options: To accept it immediately
To study it in a laboratory
To doubt that it is completely true
To compare it with your family tree

multipleChoice.question: Why should people be cautious about DNA ancestry tests?
options: They cannot use databases
They only work for people with unusual surnames
They ignore family history completely
Humans share most of their DNA with each other

multipleChoice.question: How does Louise Baldock distinguish ancestry from ethnicity?
options: Ancestry is about continents, while ethnicity is only about names
Ancestry is about actual forebears; ethnicity is more cultural and geographical
Ancestry is always less accurate than ethnicity
Ethnicity is only about parents and children

multipleChoice.question: What happened with Greg Foot's first DNA test?
options: It showed five generations from England, matching what he knew
It said he was mostly from the United States
It refused to compare his sample
It found no connection to his known family

multipleChoice.question: What was surprising about Greg's second DNA test?
options: It found no evidence of English ancestry
It said all his DNA was identical to Beth's
It proved every family record was false
It gave only one percentage: 100% English

multipleChoice.question: Why can two DNA companies give different results?
options: DNA changes after it is mailed
The same person has different DNA each day
The presenter used a fake surname
Companies compare samples with different databases

multipleChoice.question: What percentage of DNA do humans share, according to the programme?
What is the safest interpretation of these tests?
options: They are useless for all family research
They can be interesting, but results should be interpreted carefully
They always prove exact national identity
They replace all historical records
